text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on AIML-01: Absence of a design pipeline: CONFIRMED. My own `grep -nEi "rfdiffusion|proteinmpnn|bindcraft|Rosetta|ipTM|pae_interaction|docking|vina|MMGBSA|MSA"` and a separate grep for ESM returned zero hits across app.js, README.md, index.html. `git ls-files` returns exactly .gitignore, README.md, app.js, index.html, skills-lock.json, styles.css plus ~230 vendored .agents/skills/** files -- no design script, no PDB/CIF, no score table, no seed. Provenance: I downloaded the UniProt reference entries and confirmed all four exact-match claims to the residue: GRPRTTSFAESCKPVQQPSAFGSMKVSRDKDG = P49841 (GSK3B) 3-34 verbatim; APMKEANIRGQGGLAYPGVRT = P23560 (BDNF) 19-39 verbatim; KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM = P05067 (APP) 687-706 verbatim; DEETGEFL = Q16236 (NFE2L2) 77-84 verbatim. WNT3A: P56704 203-223 is CKCHGLSGSCEVKTCWWSQPD and the drug motif is CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLC -- I counted 14/21 identity, exactly as claimed. Tiling: my greedy maximal-substring tiling (min 6 aa) of the 25 drug sequences against the 10 AF3_CANDIDATES fastas gives 805/839 = 95.9% (reviewer: 801/839 = 95.5%); total residues 876 and 876-37 = 839 both reproduce exactly, so the small delta is tiling-algorithm choice, not error. BLAST: I could NOT reproduce the reviewer's specific blastp hit list (MEGF11 E=2e-05, Tenascin, Notch3, Jagged-2, Slit2) -- no BLAST was run in my session. I substituted an independent test: Smith-Waterman (BLOSUM62, gap 11/1) of each flagship sequence against its advertised target, calibrated against 30 shuffled-sequence nulls. Results fully support the reviewer's conclusion: 49-mer 'TrkB D5 binder' vs NTRK2 SW=35, z=2.3, below the shuffled maximum of 36; 41-mer vs CHRNA7 SW=33 (z=1.8) and vs TLR4 not in top 6; 31-mer 'Trem2 agonist' vs TREM2 not in top 6; 36-mer 'AChE clamper' vs ACHE indistinguishable from noise. By contrast the three genuine grafts light up unmistakably: GSK3B fragment z=44.5, APP fragment z=19.8, WNT3A fragment z=26.7. The substantive claim -- these are copied natural motifs, and the sequences bear no relation to their advertised targets -- is independently established. Correction: (1) The evidence line 'app.js:130 ... CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH' is imprecise: app.js:130 is a 40-mer, CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCHGMSGSCSTK, not the 31-mer at 173/371. (2) The BLAST hit list must be re-run and logged before issue, or downgraded to 'no significant similarity to the advertised target (verified by Smith-Waterman vs shuffled null)'; a specific E-value that the report cannot reproduce is the one thing that would let the author dismiss the whole review. (3) The tiling figure should read 805/839 = 95.9% or be stated as ~96%. (4) The NFE2L2 verbatim stretch is 8 residues (DEETGEFL, 77-84), not 12: the drug's DEETGEFLFQLP does not exist in NFE2L2, which has DEETGEFLPIQPAQ -- so even the correctly-chosen motif is garbled past residue 8, and README.md:62 presents the non-existent 12-mer as 'Nrf2 ETGE'. (5) The fix's line list is incomplete: README.md:45 contains no 'De Novo' (it says 'AlphaFold3-optimized'); index.html:54, 262 and 323 also carry 'De Novo' and are omitted; app.js:137 is omitted; and index.html:410, the footer reading 'Generated with AlphaFold3 3D Structural Modeling & Structural Pharmacology Algorithms', is the most explicit false-provenance line on the page and appears in no fix list in this review.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on AIML-02: Counts reproduce exactly: I parsed 25 `sequence:` entries yielding 21 distinct, and 25+10 = 35 entries yielding 26 distinct. The four intra-drug duplicate pairs are exactly those named. Target contradictions verified verbatim from source: SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGCDERACPRCHGFWREVC appears at app.js:195 against 'alpha7 nAChR Extracellular Domain (ECD) (Tyr188, Trp149, Tyr195)' and byte-identically at app.js:319 against 'TLR4 / MD-2 Complex (Arg264, Lys341, Glu439)'. CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH appears at app.js:173 against 'Frizzled-8 (FZD8) CRD Domain' and at app.js:371 against 'BMEC Zonula Occludens-1 (ZO-1) & Occludin Complex'. TJP1/ZO-1 is a cytoplasmic MAGUK scaffold; an extracellular Cys-rich peptide cannot reach it -- that sub-point is unassailable and is the strongest part of this finding. VRACPTGKCEGLRGYTCRCEPGWKGPDCRERACPDCH at 205 (TrkB D5) and 361 (EAAT2) confirmed. Divergent numbers for identical input confirmed: 196/198 gives dG -16.5, Kd 1.8 nM, pLDDT 93.2 while 320/322 gives -15.7, 3.8 nM, 92.8. Correction: Two reasoning errors that must be fixed before issue. (1) 'pLDDT ... is in any case a monomer confidence metric that does not depend on the binding partner at all' is FALSE as written. When AF3 predicts a complex, the per-residue pLDDT of the binder chain is computed on the complex coordinates and is influenced by the partner; a binder disordered alone and ordered at an interface genuinely scores differently. The reviewer states the correct version in their own ground_truth (pLDDT is a local-confidence metric, not an interface metric; ipTM and interface PAE are the interface metrics) -- the what_is_wrong text must be brought into line with it. (2) Following from (1), 'AF3 is deterministic for a fixed input and seed; the same sequence against the same target cannot yield two pLDDT values' does not actually apply here, because 196 and 320 are nominally two DIFFERENT complexes (alpha7 vs TLR4); real complex predictions would legitimately give two different pLDDTs. The dispositive argument is different and stronger: no target appears anywhere in the pipeline (AIML-01/03 establish that no complex was ever predicted), so a partner-dependent number cannot have been computed; and no target-conditioned generator can emit one 41-mer optimised for a Cys-loop receptor ECD and an LRR innate-immune co-receptor. As written, a knowledgeable author could refute the stated reason and, by association, dismiss a correct finding. (3) The reviewer missed the sharper internal contradiction: the SAME 36-mer KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG carries THREE different binding free energies -- dG -12.6 (app.js:131), -16.2 (app.js:156), -17.5 (app.js:250) -- and the 32-mer GSK3B graft carries -11.8 (app.js:133) vs -16.0 (app.js:228). dG, unlike pLDDT, has no partner-dependence escape hatch once you also accept that no partner structure exists. That belongs in this finding.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on AIML-03: Source quotations are exact. app.js:791 is verbatim `let score = 93 + Math.sin(i * 0.4) * 4 + (char.charCodeAt(0) % 5) * 0.5;`, app.js:850 is verbatim `let error = Math.abs(i - j) * 0.4 + (sequence.charCodeAt(i % sequence.length) % 4) * 0.3;`, app.js:707 carries the 'REAL FASTA SEQUENCE PARSING' comment, app.js:715 is `let radius = 6 + (charCode % 5) * 0.8;`, app.js:802 labels the dataset 'AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score'. I re-implemented the pLDDT generator in python3 and reproduced every reported statistic: real 36-mer mean 94.11, min 89.1, max 99.0; placeholder 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate' mean 94.09, min 89.1, max 99.0; poly-Q24 mean 94.31. PAE maximum on a 45x45 grid = 44*0.4 + 3*0.3 = 18.5 against an axis labelled '0 - 30 A' at index.html:397 -- confirmed. No fetch/XMLHttpRequest/axios in app.js -- confirmed, zero hits. index.html:42 and :363 are ordinary anchors to alphafoldserver.com -- confirmed by reading. Leaderboard/drug pLDDT contradictions 92.8 (131) / 94.8 (156) / 94.3 (250) -- confirmed exactly. The 3D generator at 711-732 and 973-991 has no phi/psi, no Ramachandran term, no vdW, no chirality -- confirmed by reading. Correction: Three factual corrections, one of which strengthens the finding. (1) 'hard-clamped to [76, 98.6]' is wrong. Those clamps at app.js:792-793 are unreachable dead code: the expression's algebraic range is 93 +/- 4 plus 0..2, i.e. [89.0, 99.0], so `score > 100` and `score < 70` never fire. The true floor is 89.0, not 76 -- the display is even less capable of expressing low confidence than the reviewer claims. State the range as [89.0, 99.0] and drop the reference to the clamps as the mechanism. (2) 'byte-for-byte the same confidence profile as the real peptide' is REFUTED. The two strings differ in length (36 vs 37) and in every per-residue value (real starts 94.6, 96.9, 97.7, 97.0; placeholder starts 95.6, 95.9, 96.7, 99.0). What is true, and is still damning, is that the rounded summary statistics are identical: mean 94.1, min 89.1, max 99.0 for both. Rewrite to 'the same mean, minimum and maximum to one decimal place'. (3) 'the 100-mer at app.js:125 ... renders as a clean diagonal' is wrong: app.js:125 is an AF3_CANDIDATES fasta and never reaches renderModalPaeHeatmap, which is called only from openDrugModal (app.js:651) with drug.sequence. The correct examples are the GGGGS-containing drug sequences at app.js:183, 235, 287, 339 and 391. (4) Minor: 'there is no network call in the codebase' overstates -- index.html:9-18 load Google Fonts, FontAwesome, three.js and Chart.js from CDNs. The precise claim is 'no AlphaFold API call anywhere in the codebase', which is what matters. (5) The fix list omits index.html:296, 347, 368 and, most importantly, the footer at index.html:410.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on AIML-04: B at 1-based position 19 in all three entries -- confirmed (app.js:130, 173, 371). app.js:381 `sequence: "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate"` -- confirmed. The AF3 input contract is verified verbatim: I fetched google-deepmind/alphafold3 docs/input.md and line 222 reads 'the 1-letter standard amino acid codes.' The delivery path is real: app.js:600 sets currentActiveModalSequence, app.js:619-621 renders it as 'FASTA Peptide / Bio-Conjugate Sequence', app.js:662 writes it to the clipboard, index.html:359 tells the user to submit it to the AlphaFold Server. The disulfide-ambiguity arithmetic checks out: app.js:143 (47-mer) and app.js:215 (45-mer) each carry exactly 8 cysteines, and 7!! = 7*5*3*1 = 105 perfect matchings. Correction: (1) The cysteine count is UNDERSTATED. I enumerated all 25 drug sequences: ten genuine peptide entries carry an odd cysteine count, not nine, and the evidence block lists only eight. The reviewer missed app.js:225 GRPRTTSFAESCKPVQQPSAFGSMKVSRDKDG (1 Cys) and app.js:339 GRLVGHPWECDRGGGGSDEETGEWRWYCPWC (3 Cys). Correct list: 173 (7), 205 (7), 225 (1), 267 (5), 287 (5), 299 (5), 339 (3), 351 (5), 361 (7), 371 (7). (2) The quoted string for app.js:130 is wrong -- that line holds the 40-mer ...ACPDCHGMSGSCSTK, not the 31-mer. (3) The fix contains a concrete error that would be implemented as written: 'WNT3A carries L at the aligned position, so B->L' is FALSE. B sits at motif position 19, which aligns to WNT3A Gln221 (P56704 203-223 = CKCHGLSGSCEVKTCWWSQPD; position 19 is Q, position 6 is the L the reviewer appears to have read off). B->L would install a residue that is wrong at that position and would change the cysteine-independent character of the C-terminal segment. Either B->Q with the WNT3A alignment stated, or -- better, given AIML-01 -- delete the entries.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on AIML-05: All four sub-claims verified against downloaded UniProt entries. (a) app.js:277 KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLMGGGSGGSGRLVGHPW -- I located KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM at P05067 687-706 exactly, i.e. Abeta(16-35) given Abeta1 = APP672; app.js:282 does describe it as disrupting 'Abeta-AChE amyloid fibril seeding', README.md:77 calls it an 'Abeta Disruptor' and app.js:281 asserts 'Fibril Blockade: 100%'. Abeta16-35 contains KLVFF plus the entire hydrophobic C-terminal stretch and is the nucleating core; presenting it as the inhibitor inverts the direction of effect. This is the one finding in the report with a physical hazard attached. (b) app.js:225 is P49841 3-34 verbatim, and I confirmed it contains Ser9 (GSK3B = M-S-G-R-P-R-T-T-S...). The mechanistic objection is correct: the phospho-Ser9 N-terminal tail is an intramolecular pseudosubstrate for the primed-phosphate groove, not an ATP-competitive ligand, and a 32-mer (~3.5 kDa) cannot occupy an adenine cleft that accommodates ~500 Da. (c) P23560 residues 19-39 = APMKEANIRGQGGLAYPGVRT confirmed; I also confirmed the mature chain begins at 129 (P23560 129- = HSDPARRGELSVCDSISEWVTA). (d) TJP1/ZO-1 is cytoplasmic -- an extracellular Cys-rich peptide cannot engage it. My Smith-Waterman screen independently supports the grafts being what the reviewer says they are (APP z=19.8, GSK3B z=44.5, WNT3A z=26.7 against a shuffled null). Correction: (1) P23560 1-18 is the signal peptide and 19-128 the propeptide, so residues 19-39 lie wholly within the prodomain; 'signal-peptide/prodomain region' is loose and should read 'prodomain (propeptide 19-128)'. The substantive point -- not mature BDNF, opposite pharmacology via p75NTR/sortilin-family co-receptors -- stands, but note the review offers no retrieved citation for the prodomain-signalling claim; either add one or state it as established textbook pharmacology. (2) The reviewer's aside that the Nrf2 ETGE at app.js:127/163 shows 'the author can pick correct motifs when the biology is simple' needs qualifying: only DEETGEFL (NFE2L2 77-84) is verbatim. The construct's DEETGEFLFQLP does not occur in NFE2L2 (the natural sequence continues DEETGEFLPIQPAQ), and README.md:62 presents that non-existent 12-mer as the 'Nrf2 ETGE'. The one motif held up as correctly handled is itself wrong past residue 8.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED on AIML-06: The category error is correct on the merits: AF3 maps (sequence, ligands, MSA) to coordinates plus confidence heads, with no inverse-folding head, no backbone diffusion over sequence space and no free-energy function, so nothing can be 'designed via AlphaFold3' or 'AlphaFold3-optimized'. I verified the framing text at README.md:22 and :45, index.html:265-266 and :290, and the page title at index.html:6. The thermodynamics reproduce EXACTLY, digit for digit. With RT = 0.0019872041 * 298.15 = 0.5925 kcal/mol and dG = RT ln(Kd), all 25 rows parsed cleanly: implied dG spans -11.35 to -13.77 against stated -15.2 to -19.5; the offset spans 3.85 to 5.73 kcal/mol; every one of the 25 offsets has the same sign; and the -19.5 row (app.js:290, Kd 0.08 nM) implies -13.77 while -19.5 would imply Kd = 5.09 fM. The reviewer's numbers are precise. Absence of filter metrics confirmed by grep (zero hits for ipTM, pae_interaction, RMSD, ddG). The 25/25 success pattern confirmed: every Kd < 5 nM (max 4.8), every pLDDT > 92 (min 92.4 at app.js:384), 'hERG IC50 > 50 uM' on all 25 safety strings, 'Off-target Binding: None' at app.js:209, 'Fibril Blockade: 100%' at app.js:281. Literature: I verified Cao et al. via PubMed efetch and the abstract contains the reviewer's quotation verbatim -- 'Experimental data on nearly half a million computational designs and hundreds of thousands of point mutants' -- plus '12 diverse protein targets' and crystal structures of five complexes. I verified the AlphaProteo blog by fetching it: 'seven target proteins we tested', '3 to 300 times better binding affinities', 88% for BHRF1, and the explicit TNF-alpha failure as the 8th target. I fetched martinpacesa/BindCraft settings_filters/default_filters.json and every threshold the reviewer quotes is exact: Average_i_pAE 0.35 (lower-is-better), Average_i_pTM 0.5, Average_pLDDT 0.8, Average_ShapeComplementarity 0.6, Average_dG 0, Average_Surface_Hydrophobicity 0.35, Average_n_InterfaceUnsatHbonds 4. Correction: Two sub-claims I could not verify in this session and which should be marked or dropped: the '9%' lower bound of AlphaProteo's 9-88% range does not appear on the cited blog URL (88%, seven targets, 3-300x and the TNF-alpha failure all do), and Bennett et al.'s 'roughly ten-fold' improvement was not confirmed against the paper text. Both are almost certainly right, but a report whose thesis is fabricated numbers cannot carry an unverified number. Also: the reviewer's 'the 25 dG values are not AF3 output under any interpretation' would be sharper paired with the observation that the same sequence carries three different dG values across the dataset (-12.6/-16.2/-17.5 for the 36-mer), which forecloses the 'computed by some other tool' defence.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: BINDING-SITE RESIDUE NUMBERING MIXES TWO ORGANISMS INSIDE A SINGLE STRING. app.js:154 reads 'AChE CAS (Trp84, Phe330, Tyr121) & PAS (Trp286, Tyr72, Tyr341)'; app.js:248 repeats the pattern. I checked these against human ACHE (P22303, 614 aa, signal peptide 1-31): in mature human numbering position 84 is Glu, 330 is Val and 121 is Gly, whereas 286 is Trp, 72 is Tyr and 341 is Tyr. Trp84/Phe330/Tyr121 are Torpedo californica numbering (human equivalents Trp86/Phe338/Tyr124, which I confirmed are W/F/Y). So the catalytic-site residues are Torpedo and the peripheral-site residues in the same parenthesis are human. The project is internally inconsistent too: app.js:12 gives 'Trp279 (PAS)' (Torpedo) while README.md:32 gives 'PAS (Trp286)' (human). Any of the residue-level annotations across all 25 entries should be presumed unchecked until re-verified against a stated reference numbering.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: NO TARGET STRUCTURE EXISTS ANYWHERE, WHICH IS THE PRECONDITION THE WHOLE DISCIPLINE TURNS ON. There is not one PDB ID, mmCIF, hotspot-residue set derived from a structure, or epitope definition in the repository. Target-conditioned design (RFdiffusion, BindCraft, AlphaProteo) begins with target coordinates plus hotspots; without them there is nothing to condition on, so the absence is not merely undocumented provenance -- it makes the claimed activity impossible in principle rather than merely unevidenced. The review argues from the absence of outputs (design PDBs, score CSVs, seeds); the absence of the required input is the stronger and more easily explained argument.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: ZERO DEVELOPABILITY OR LIABILITY FILTERING, ON A SET WHERE THE LIABILITIES ARE VISIBLE FROM THE SEQUENCE. The 36-mer KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG (app.js:131/153/247) has 13 K/R against 4 D/E, net charge about +9, with 4 Trp, 4 Phe and 6 Leu -- a textbook cationic amphipathic architecture of the cell-penetrating/membrane-lytic class, not a selective enzyme binder. It is shipped with 'hERG IC50 > 50 uM (0% Cardiotoxicity)' and 'Peripheral Side Effects: None' (app.js:251). No aggregation propensity, no MHC-II immunogenicity prediction, no hemolysis or membrane-lysis assessment, no protease-stability consideration appears anywhere, yet README.md:101 asserts 'Low Immunogenicity'. For a reviewer whose stated speciality is in-silico filtering, the complete absence of a developability filter set -- and a safety claim that is plausibly inverted for the most-reused sequence in the dataset -- is the omission a referee would notice first.

Every one of the 25 entries is a multi-kilodalton, often highly charged peptide conjugate assigned to a specific brain region and cell type, and not one line of the repository addresses blood-brain-barrier penetration, route of administration, or CNS PK -- while README.md:90 and app.js:369-377 go so far as to name a BBB tight-junction target. The platform's entire organising principle (5 brain regions) presupposes the one property it never examines.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: THE PAE GENERATOR HAS TWO FURTHER DEFECTS WORTH NAMING IN THE FIX. app.js:850 indexes the character term by row only -- charCodeAt(i % len), never j -- so PAE(i,j) != PAE(j,i) by construction and the 'sequence-driven' contribution is a constant per row, not a pairwise quantity at all. Separately, app.js:844 caps the grid at Math.min(len, 45), so the 47-mer at app.js:143 silently renders only its first 45 residues, and neither axis is labelled with residue indices. If the panel is retained in any form these must be fixed alongside the relabelling.
